summary: Backend-only testing of StayOS Phase-1B reservation lifecycle (confirm/cancel/no-show + centralized transition map) against http://localhost:3001/api/v1. Created /app/backend/tests/test_reservation_lifecycle.py with 32 pytest cases: confirm happy path + snapshot capture/freeze, cancel (with/without reason, room release), no-show, illegal transitions from every terminal state, RBAC (readonly 403, unauthenticated 401), DTO whitelist, and full regression flow (assign -> unassign -> reassign -> check-in -> extend -> check-out with confirm/cancel/no-show rejected at CHECKED_IN and CHECKED_OUT). 29 passed, 3 failed. All confirm/cancel/no-show endpoints behave exactly as specified (200 on valid, 400 INVALID_RESERVATION_STATE_TRANSITION on every illegal/terminal transition). The 3 failures expose a bypass: the generic PATCH /reservations/:id endpoint still writes reservation.status directly, ignoring the canonical transition map.

critical.issue: Lifecycle bypass: UpdateReservationDto = PartialType(CreateReservationDto) so `status` is accepted and merged straight into the entity (reservations.service.ts update() -> toUpdatePersistenceFields). Verified: CONFIRMED -> CHECKED_OUT accepted with 200, and a terminal CANCELLED reservation was revived to CONFIRMED with 200. assertReservationTransition is never called on this path, so ALLOWED_RESERVATION_TRANSITIONS is NOT the single source of truth.

minor.issue: Duplicate ad-hoc cancel path in reservations.service.ts update() (lines 235-246): throws BadRequestException with a plain string (surfaces as VALIDATION_ERROR, not INVALID_RESERVATION_STATE_TRANSITION), does not clear roomId (no inventory release) and emits no audit/activity events, unlike ReservationWorkflowService.terminate().

policySnapshot / taxSnapshot are persisted in Postgres (verified via psql: groupDeposit + GST 12.00 with capturedAt) but are not exposed in any API response, so clients cannot read the frozen deposit/tax snapshot. Snapshot immutability had to be verified at DB level.

CreateReservationDto accepts any ReservationStatus, so a reservation can be created directly in CHECKED_IN/CHECKED_OUT/NO_SHOW, skipping the lifecycle entirely (useful for seeding, but an unguarded write path).

These paths still use ad-hoc guards (ensureReservationStatus -> RESERVATION_NOT_CHECKED_IN / RESERVATION_NOT_CONFIRMED, moveRoom -> INVALID_STATE) rather than assertReservationTransition. Behaviour is correct (400) but error codes are inconsistent with the new canonical code.

action_items: Route status changes in ReservationsService.update() through assertReservationTransition (or strip `status` from UpdateReservationDto and force clients to use the lifecycle endpoints) - currently any status jump, including reviving CANCELLED/CHECKED_OUT, is accepted with 200.

Delete the duplicate cancel branch in ReservationsService.update() and delegate to ReservationWorkflowService.cancel() so room release + audit/activity events + INVALID_RESERVATION_STATE_TRANSITION code are consistent.
Expose policySnapshot/taxSnapshot in ReservationResponseDto (read-only) so the frozen deposit/tax can be verified and rendered by clients.
Optionally migrate check-in/check-out/extend/move-room guards onto assertReservationTransition for one canonical error code.
critical_code_review_comments: reservations.service.ts:235-246 + 281-285 - generic PATCH writes ReservationStatus without transition validation; this is the only remaining hole in the Phase-1B 'single source of truth' guarantee.
ReservationsMapper.toResponse omits policy_snapshot/tax_snapshot even though they are the immutable contract captured at confirmation.

terminate() clearing roomId is correct as an inventory release hook, but there is no explicit inventory/availability recompute - fine today because rooms only turn OCCUPIED at check-in; worth a comment/test when real inventory holds land.

success_rate.backend: 90% (29/32 pytest cases; 3 failures are the generic-PATCH lifecycle bypass)

seed_data_creation: ~25 TEST reservations created via POST /reservations (notes='TEST_lifecycle') for guest fixtures; most were driven to CANCELLED/NO_SHOW/CHECKED_OUT terminal states and left in place (no delete endpoint exists). One demo guest's registration contact fields (mobile/email/address/purposeOfVisit) were updated by the check-in regression test with randomized values.
test_credentials: admin@stayos.local / Password123! (login is HTTP 201, token at data.accessToken); readonly@stayos.local / Password123! for RBAC 403 checks
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run: cd /app/backend && python -m pytest tests/test_reservation_lifecycle.py -p no:xdist -v. API base is http://localhost:3001/api/v1 (not 8001). PENDING reservations must be created via POST with status=PENDING (create defaults to CONFIRMED). Snapshots are only observable via psql (PGPASSWORD='StayOS@2026' psql -h localhost -U stayos -d stayos_dev) - helper _snapshots() in the test file. Check-in requires guest registration (incl. purposeOfVisit), verified identity with a valid PASSPORT format (e.g. M1234567) and payment review, plus arrival date <= today; unique mobile/email needed to avoid 409 CONFLICT. TestGenericPatchStatusBypass is the only failing class - re-run it after the main agent guards status changes on PATCH /reservations/:id.
rca_of_the_issue: ALLOWED_RESERVATION_TRANSITIONS/assertReservationTransition is only invoked from ReservationWorkflowService (confirm/cancel/markNoShow). The generic update endpoint copies the whole DTO (which inherits `status` from CreateReservationDto via PartialType) into the entity through toUpdatePersistenceFields and saves it, so any client with bookings.manage can set an arbitrary status. Reproduce: create reservation with status CONFIRMED, PATCH /properties/{propertyId}/reservations/{id} body {"status":"CHECKED_OUT"} -> 200; cancel a reservation then PATCH {"status":"CONFIRMED"} -> 200. Mitigation: validate with assertReservationTransition inside update(), or remove `status` from UpdateReservationDto.
